claims.statement: The run-level machine is five micro-states — 立局, 协调, 盘点, 发布, retired — and retires only on an armed `review.note`; every other transition is an effect-driven self-loop or a phase advance.
`charter.set` is available only while the charter phase is open and may be revised repeatedly; after `run.begin` it is refused readably, which is what locks the charter for the rest of the run.
`verify.submit(false)` returns the whole batch to coordination and clears the settlement and release keys, so rework is a full re-pass rather than an in-place reversal.

Once the four settlement steps are complete the run enters release by effect, without a new event, and `review.note` requires a release declaration first — a confirmed merge or an explicit skip reason.

An unarmed `review.note` settles the batch — clearing the release keys and incrementing the batch counter — while an armed one retires the run; the two endings are distinguished by the `run.retire` flag, not by wording.

Batch settlement registers `docs.maintenance.due=<batch>` in the same handler transaction and creates no requirement row; the obligation closes only by `config.set docs.maintenance.done=<batch>` or the next `coordinate.submit` blocks.
